W3 (cost lens), after E017. The tip is E017. It is E016's recipe made break-free: Muon (3 Newton-Schulz steps, no weight decay inside muon_update), Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, widths 128/384/512, label smoothing 0.3, weight decay 0.006 on the SGD groups, and 9.5 true epochs (238 steps), compiled in max-autotune with CUDA graphs. It runs in 6.548 s at 0.7537.

Key update: E017 kept the same math as E016 but moved accuracy by -0.70 pp (0.7607 → 0.7537), for -0.5% time. The reshuffle from a compile or kernel change is therefore as large as ±0.7 pp, much larger than I had assumed. E016's +0.33 pp weight-decay gain and E015's +0.27 pp gain are both inside that band. My best estimate of the recipe's true 3-seed mean is about 0.756 ± 0.003. The margin over 0.753 is about 0.3 pp in expectation and close to zero on the measured tip, so any trim must pay for itself almost entirely in accuracy, and none can afford a loss.

Time budget: time ≈ F + V × average pixel fraction.
- F is about 0.7 s; V is about 7.6 s at full 32 px.
- The current average pixel fraction is about 0.755.
- Host overhead is under 1%, so systems levers are exhausted (E015, E017).
- Approximate per-sample conv cost in MACs: group 1 about 93M, group 2 about 240M (52%), group 3 about 129M; about 460M in total.
- Group 2 at 320 channels saves about 16% of FLOPs, roughly 0.5-0.6 s.
- Dropping group 1's third conv saves about 7% of FLOPs, roughly 0.3-0.4 s with memory traffic included.

Measured prices:
- Epochs: about 2 s/pp.
- Last-group width: about 1.6 s/pp (E010).
- Aggressive resizing: 0.9 s/pp (E011, a bad trade; the 32 px tail length is critical).
- Lookahead: about +1 pp (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp (E006).
- Resizing: -22% time at about 0 pp (E007).
- Hyperparameter nudges: all inside the noise band.

Mechanisms:
1. Endpoint averaging plus the Lookahead fast-weight reset gives about 1 pp (E005).
2. Accuracy is set mostly in the 32 px tail (E011 compared with E007). Cheap early steps matter less but not nothing. Swapping 28 px for 24 px (I029) or adding a 20 px phase (I035) are the cheapest trims, about 0.2-0.35 s each at an expected 0.1-0.3 pp.
3. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry (E010), so cutting width costs more than 1 s/pp.
4. Muon renormalizes filters every step and applies no weight decay, so filter weight decay is inert. The E016 change was effectively a change to the SGD groups only.

Noise:
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed standard error is about 0.17 pp.
- Recompiling or changing kernels reshuffles accuracy by up to ±0.7 pp.
- Time noise is about 1%.

Unsure:
- Whether a fresh rebuild of identical code reselects the same kernels.
- The 40-seed mean, which is likely about 0.755.
- Whether any trim can keep the measured value at or above 0.753. Given the slim margin, many will fail by luck.

forecasts.reason: Moving 30% of steps from 28 px to 24 px saves about 0.25-0.3 s at an expected cost of about 0.2 pp, which is in the noise; it is a coin flip on clearing 0.753.
E017 shows reshuffles of up to 0.7 pp; I expect the 10-seed mean to be about 0.755, below the hypothesis's 0.757 and below 0.7607 by more than the 0.05-0.3 pp offset it predicts.
A 1-epoch cut costs about 0.5-0.8 pp, and the tip has almost no margin.
Saves about 16% of FLOPs, but CIFAR-100 is width-hungry; I expect a loss of 0.4-0.8 pp, more than the 0.25 pp the hypothesis allows.
Filter weight decay is inert, so this is a nudge to the SGD groups inside the noise; it is unlikely to reach E016's 0.7607 + 0.2 pp.
Only about 7% of FLOPs, so the time cut is probably under 8%, and accuracy loses about 0.3 pp.
A 20 px phase over 15% of steps saves about 0.15-0.2 s, under the 4% the hypothesis needs; the accuracy change is in the noise.

cruxes: What is the true 10-seed mean of the tip recipe: about 0.757 (real margin to spend) or about 0.754 (no margin, so every trim fails)?
Does rebuilding identical code reselect the same kernels (bit-identical results), or does each build reshuffle accuracy by ±0.5 pp? This decides whether 3-seed keep decisions mean anything.
Is the per-step cost at 24 px much lower than at 28 px on the A100, or does low-resolution inefficiency eat the saving from the 28→24 swap?
